reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with Borel measurable structure and canonical Lebesgue volume, permitting dimension zero. The approved ambient section instances are part of the contract. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume exp(-W) is Lebesgue integrable. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), i.e. the measure with density exp(-W)/integral exp(-W) relative to volume; positive normalization is not built into that definition.
For every real-linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E), assume D is closable and its graph is exactly characterized as follows: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H,
  (a,H) belongs to graph(D) if and only if there exists a smooth compactly supported phi:E->R with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) mu-almost everywhere.
D.closure is the operator with that same topological graph closure, on its submodule domain. This D is fixed before epsilon and the forcing f.
For every real epsilon>0 and every f in L2(mu;R), there exists u in D.closure.domain satisfying all conclusions below simultaneously. Write u_rep and f_rep for the standard measurable representatives of the actual scalar L2 classes, and G_rep for the standard representative of G=D.closure(u) in L2(mu;E). Abbreviate the exact scalar expression by
  r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x).
(a) For every z in D.closure.domain,
  epsilon*<u,z>_{L2(mu;R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(z)>_{L2(mu;E)}=<f,z>_{L2(mu;R)}.
(b) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to Lebesgue volume.
(c) For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every direction a in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
(d) The real scalar function x->||r(x)||^2 is locally Lebesgue integrable.
(e) For every compact set K in E, u_rep, G_rep and r each satisfy MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to volume.restrict K, including a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm for that actual restricted measure.
(f) For every C2 compactly supported phi:E->R, the two functions x->u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) and x->r(x)*phi(x) are Lebesgue integrable and
  integral u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) dx = integral r(x)*phi(x) dx.
(g) For every C2 compactly supported chi:E->R, define the following actual functions, with the notation v_chi corresponding to the let-defined v in the statement:
  v_chi(x)=chi(x)*u_rep(x),
  G_chi(x)=chi(x) scalar-multiplied by G_rep(x) + u_rep(x) scalar-multiplied by gradient(chi)(x),
  F_chi(x)=chi(x)*r(x)+2*<gradient(chi)(x),G_rep(x)>_E+u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(chi)(x).
Then v_chi, G_chi and F_chi each satisfy MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to the full volume measure, with actual a.e. strong measurability and finite global L2 norm. All three topological supports are contained in the topological support of chi:
  tsupport(v_chi) subset tsupport(chi),
  tsupport(G_chi) subset tsupport(chi),
  tsupport(F_chi) subset tsupport(chi).
For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every a in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E and x->v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E dx = - integral v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For every C2 compactly supported phi:E->R, both x->v_chi(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) and x->F_chi(x)*phi(x) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral v_chi(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) dx = integral F_chi(x)*phi(x) dx.
All unannotated local-integrability, integrability and integral assertions use canonical Lebesgue volume. The Hilbert inner products use the actual law mu. Laplacian.laplacian on chi and phi is the actual finite-basis test-function trace; no classical Laplacian of the arbitrary representative u_rep or v_chi is asserted. The same u and G serve every test and every cutoff. chi is any real C2 compact-support function, without positivity, value-range or plateau assumptions. The localized functions are given by these three formulas, not independent existential choices; no membership of v_chi in a weighted partial-operator domain is asserted.
The result is a universal implication for any such supplied D; it does not add a dense-domain premise or assert existence of D. One u is selected per epsilon,f before all compact restrictions, ordinary tests and cutoffs. No solution uniqueness, H2 regularity, classical Delta u, core characterization, measurable parameter selection or quantitative bound is an explicit conclusion.
objects: C1 potential W, normalized tilt mu, arbitrary supplied closable scalar-to-vector L2(mu) partial gradient D with exact graph, its closure, epsilon>0 and scalar L2 forcing f; actual representative u_rep of the selected closure-domain solution and actual G_rep of closureD(u); r=epsilon*u_rep+<gradient W,G_rep>-f_rep; all compact K, ordinary tests, C2 cutoffs and formula-defined localized v_chi,G_chi,F_chi.
domains: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E with canonical volume, including dimension zero. Scalar and vector Lp at exponent 2 are actual L2 quotients, whose coercions are the standard measurable representatives. D is a real-linear partial operator on a submodule domain; u and variational tests belong to D.closure.domain. Original G is the actual representative of D.closure(u), not a separately selected weak-gradient witness. Unannotated integrability and integrals use volume; compact L2 restrictions explicitly use volume.restrict K. Localized v_chi,F_chi:E->R and G_chi:E->E are actual formula-defined functions with global MemLp 2 volume. C1 gradient tests and C2 PDE tests/cutoffs have compact topological support. Laplacian of test/cutoff is the actual finite-basis trace. Hilbert inner products and the original scalar/vector quotient classes are under mu=volume.tilted(-W), not volume.
quantifiers: Universal ambient E/W subject to C1 and exp(-W) volume-integrability; let mu; forall D then closability and exact graph-iff premises. Graph-iff is forall scalar a/vector H with exists smooth compact-support generator. Then forall real epsilon, epsilon>0 -> forall scalar L2 f, exists u. This u precedes all variational v, ordinary C1 psi/all directions, compact K, ordinary C2 phi, and all C2 compact-support cutoffs chi. Each chi binds three lets v,Gchi,Fchi, then all localized C1 psi/all directions and all localized C2 phi. There is one D before epsilon/f and one u before every cutoff. No localized existential unknown is introduced.
assumptions: Approved finite-dimensional real inner-product/Borel ambient instances, including zero dimension; W C1; exp(-W) volume-integrable; supplied D closable and graph exactly the smooth compact-support scalar/gradient classes modulo mu. epsilon>0 antecedent; f actual scalar L2(mu). Tests have the stated C1/C2 and compact support conditions; K IsCompact. Cutoffs have only C2 and compact support, no range or plateau requirement. No dense-domain hypothesis or D existence premise, no mean-zero forcing, no added C2 W assumption.
conclusion: One selected closure-domain u satisfies the Hilbert variational equation for all closure-domain tests; volume local integrability of original u_rep/G_rep; for every C1 compact test and every direction the two L1 products and ordinary weak-gradient equation with minus sign; local volume integrability of ||r||^2; MemLp 2 (volume.restrict K) for u_rep,G_rep,r for every compact K; for every C2 compact test the two L1 products and unweighted positive-sign equation integral u_rep*Delta(phi)=integral r*phi. For every C2 compact cutoff chi, let v_chi=chi*u_rep, G_chi=chi scalar-multiplied by G_rep + u_rep scalar-multiplied by gradient chi, and F_chi=chi*r + 2*<gradient chi,G_rep> + u_rep*Delta chi. All three are actual global MemLp 2 volume and each topological support is contained in tsupport chi. For every C1 compact psi and direction a, both psi*<G_chi,a> and v_chi*Dpsi[a] are volume-integrable and integral psi*<G_chi,a>=-integral v_chi*Dpsi[a]. For every C2 compact phi both v_chi*Delta phi and F_chi*phi are volume-integrable and integral v_chi*Delta phi=integral F_chi*phi. Every integrability assertion is retained separately from the equations. r uses gradient W; this conclusion is conditional on the universal supplied D.
scopes: All original and localized blocks concern the same u and actual closure output G. L2 Hilbert law mu is distinct from volume local/distribution/global-localization measures. Original graph equalities are mu-a.e. and conclusions about actual representatives use the approved standard coercions. r is only shorthand for the exact displayed residual. Localized lets are scoped under forall chi after existential u; support assertions are inclusions, not equalities. Localization gives global volume L2 of formula-defined functions, not their membership in D or D.closure weighted domain. No classical Delta u/v_chi, H2 regularity, core theorem, measurable selection, solution uniqueness, or quantitative bound is asserted.
constant_dependencies: epsilon arbitrary strictly positive real. Residual coefficients are +epsilon,+1,-1. Localization has exact +1 coefficient on chi*r, exact positive 2 on <gradient chi,G>, exact +1 on u*Delta chi, and both product-rule gradient coefficients are 1. Norm-squared and all MemLp exponents are exactly 2. mu depends on W; D is supplied before epsilon/f; u may depend on W,D,epsilon,f; localized objects depend on that same u,G and chi, not tests. No unspecified bound or cutoff constraint.
